editorial:
Imagine waking up to find out your entire country is about to go broke. That is exactly what happens in this tense ride. You follow Han Shi-hyun, a smart guy at the Bank of Korea who realizes the government is lying about how much money they actually have. He joins a secret crisis team to try and stop the crash, but he quickly learns that some people in power actually want the system to fail so they can make a profit. It feels like a ticking clock is running in the background, making you feel the panic of the regular people losing their life savings while the rich guys play games with the economy.

The acting is top-notch and keeps you glued to the screen, even when they are talking about boring money stuff. The movie does a great job of showing the difference between the fancy offices and the struggling streets. While some of the financial talk might get a bit heavy, the human drama makes it work. It is a great pick for anyone who likes true stories about greed and power.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that while the government eventually got a bailout from the IMF, the cost was huge for the average person. Many people lost their jobs and homes, while the greedy investors who bet against the country became rich. The final scenes show that the system did not really change. You see that the same kinds of financial risks still happen today, leaving you with a chilling feeling that history repeats itself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about money, power, and government secrets.
